A second per lap. In armor racing, on this Kamakura circuit, an overwhelming margin.

Against Yokomori Forge's Super Hound, no less. A machine that has conquered the world, even if with a foreign rider aboard.

Look: Yokotan Works has brought its machine back out. ...Pointless, surely. Meaningless also. Beat Ultima in qualifying or fail to, tomorrow's contest remains undecided. A good starting position secured, they need only observe the opposition now.

So I think. Yet their feelings, I believe I understand.

Confusion. Probably enough to rob them of sound judgment.

Fellow gambling proponents or not, most likely nobody told them about this machine. Perhaps they meant to snatch victory and take the lead once gambling began. That dream has crumbled; they cannot accept it yet.

Like people rereading their exam results, certain the university must have misprinted something.

Otherwise, that beauty could not exist. Not the unthinking beauty of a rocky mountain, shaped by wind and rain over thousands of years. The very opposite.

A sculptor with blind, excessive faith in his own power. Carves an ordinary stone, keeps carving, changes it beyond its original shape—and finally makes his delusion real, turns it into a shining jewel.

An entirely tyrannical art.
